investigator.method: Level 1 PASSIVE_STATIC only: plain curl GET (descriptive User-Agent, no authentication, no browser, no JS execution) of the venue's official homepage, which embeds its own full programme as a server-rendered accordion listing 18 real upcoming event rows directly in the HTML — no separate programme page exists to fetch. The page's own JSON-LD block (Yoast SEO plugin) is WebSite/WebPage/BreadcrumbList schema only, not Event schema, and was inspected and ruled out rather than assumed absent.

probe_history.reason: A plain curl GET of https://www.renate.cc/ (the venue's own domain — renate.cc redirects to it, HTTP 301) returned a fully server-rendered '#program' accordion embedded directly on the homepage: 18 real upcoming event rows, each with day, date (DD.MM., no year), title, category, and often a room-level text breakdown (GARDEN/GREEN/BLACK/RED — this venue's own known named spaces). This directly answers the investigation question at Level 1 for the fields the source actually exposes; no JSON-LD Event schema, ICS, WordPress REST calendar API, Fourvenues, or Sanity signature was present (the one JSON-LD block found is generic Yoast SEO WebSite/WebPage schema, not Event data — confirmed by inspection, not assumed). No structural/browser escalation was needed to reach this conclusion; what remains missing (a stated year, a per-event permalink) is a genuine source limitation, not something a deeper technical probe would resolve.

venue_reference: Wilde Renate / Salon zur wilden Renate (club, Alt Stralau 70, Berlin-Friedrichshain, near S-Bahn Ostkreuz/Treptower Park — address per the venue's own retained 'Directions and Public Transport' text, see identity.notes — named indoor/outdoor spaces including GARDEN, GREEN, BLACK, RED rooms)

identity.notes: renate.cc is independently corroborated as the venue's own domain by multiple third-party discovery sources (Berlin.de, Top10Berlin, regioactive.de — treated only as a discovery lead), and the retained page content itself (its own <title>'Renate', its own JSON-LD WebSite name 'Renate', its own community/house-rules text referring to itself as 'Renate' throughout) is the actual first-party evidence of identity. Re-verified live on 2026-08-26 (ev-homepage-full-reverify): the homepage's own 'House Rules' accordion section, item 10 ('Directions and Public Transport'), states the venue's own physical address directly as first-party text: 'Alt Stralau 70, Berlin-Friedrichshain, S-Bahn station Ostkreuz or S-Bahn station Treptower Park' — confirming and refining venue_reference's 'near Ostkreuz' description with a cited, retained, first-party street address. This address is recorded here as evidenced text only; it was NOT geocoded and no coordinates were derived from it.

site_classification.platform: WordPress (X-Redirect-By: WordPress response header on the www redirect, PHP/7.4.33, Yoast SEO plugin present) with a custom theme rendering the entire programme as a static accordion directly on the homepage — no wp-content/wp-json paths were found in the retained HTML itself, and no dedicated calendar plugin signature was present.

title.notes: Each programme row's own 'prog-title' div text, sampled directly (event dated 16.10.).

start_date.notes: Each row's own 'prog-date' div states day and month directly (e.g. '16.10.') — but NO year is stated anywhere in or near the programme section, and no month/year heading governs the list (unlike the policy's worked DETERMINISTIC_CONTEXT example of a 'September 2026' heading over day-only cards). The 18 sampled rows run chronologically from 15.08. to 29.10. with no wraparound, which would make 2026 a very plausible year given today's date — but per docs/SOURCE_INVESTIGATION_POLICY.md's explicit worked example ('Today is August 2026; card says "17 September"; no page/section/year context' -> AI_INFERENCE, stays AMBIGUOUS/UNKNOWN), that plausibility is exactly the forbidden basis. Recorded PARTIAL (day/month genuinely proven, year genuinely unresolved) rather than guessed.

time.notes: Not stated for most rows. One sampled row (the recurring Renate Garden listing) states room-level open times directly as text ('GARDEN (from 14:00)', 'GREEN (from 22:00)') but most club-night rows state no time at all.

end.notes: No end/closing time is stated for any sampled row.

venue_location.notes: Not uniform across rows: some events (e.g. the recurring Renate Garden listing) break location down by the venue's own named spaces (GARDEN/GREEN/BLACK/RED) as plain text; most other sampled rows state no location breakdown at all beyond the page's own overall venue context. Recorded PARTIAL rather than generalised into a uniform per-event pattern.

source_record_id.notes: Renate's own site exposes no per-event permalink, slug, or numeric ID at all — events exist only as rows within one shared accordion on the homepage, not as separate pages. The only per-event identifier anywhere is embedded in each row's outbound 'Tickets' link, which points to a third-party platform (Resident Advisor, e.g. 'https://de.ra.co/events/2355667') and carries RA's own event ID, not Renate's. Documenting this honestly as the alternative-identity option per docs/SOURCE_INVESTIGATION_POLICY.md's activation gate 6: a future collector could use the RA numeric ID purely as a de-duplication key (never as a first-party fact source for date/price), but that decision is out of scope for this investigation and is NOT claimed PROVEN here.

event_url.notes: No per-event detail page exists on renate.cc itself — only the shared homepage accordion and an outbound third-party ticket link (Resident Advisor) per row.

price.notes: No price figure is stated on any sampled row — only 'Tickets are available on Resident Advisor and at the door', with a note that the venue is fully cashless (card only) at the door.

blockers.description: No year is stated anywhere in or near the programme section, so a real collector cannot honestly resolve start_date to a full calendar date from this source alone — it would need an external, independently-evidenced year-assignment strategy (e.g. cross-referencing the linked Resident Advisor event page, which is out of scope for this investigation) rather than assuming the current year.
No first-party per-event identifier or permalink exists on this domain at all — every candidate identifier available (the RA ticket-link ID) originates from a third party, not from Renate's own site.
